title: Rosalind and the Compass
premise: During a bitter border war in an unnamed 19th-century European province, battlefield nurse Jonah Vane keeps a hidden ledger of soldiers erased from official rolls—men whose deaths would embarrass their commanders. When census taker Rosalind Ashe arrives at his field hospital and asks one question too many, Jonah realizes she is hunting the ledger for reasons of her own: her brother's name is among the omitted. Together they must smuggle the book past three military checkpoints to the capital's war tribunal, testing whether loyalty to comrades, to truth, or to each other will survive. The story ends at the third checkpoint, where Jonah surrenders himself so Rosalind can carry the ledger through—and where his own name, it turns out, was written on its final page all along.
about_author: Orsen Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from provincial wars before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse library where he keeps, he admits, one ledger of his own.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Jonah Vane's POV. In a muddy field hospital, Jonah records the names of dead men absent from official dispatches, hiding the ledger beneath a loose floorboard. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as routine, establishing his compulsion to make the invisible count.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dawn
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A retreat is ordered; the hospital must evacuate with only what can be carried. Jonah must choose what to abandon—the ledger cannot fit in his kit without sacrificing medicine. Beat: first moral fracture between duty and truth.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counted
chapters.summary: Rosalind Ashe's POV. The census taker arrives at the makeshift hospital near the river town of Halven, methodical and watchful, asking about missing personnel. Beat: unease; Jonah recognizes a hunter when he sees one.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Over tea, Rosalind probes Jonah about a soldier named Elias Ashe—her brother, listed as deserted. Jonah lies badly. Beat: two secrets collide; both leave the conversation knowing more than they admitted.

chapters.title: What the Floorboard Kept
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah discovers someone searched his quarters; the ledger is disturbed but intact. He decides to move it that night. Beat: paranoia takes root; trust becomes a currency he can no longer afford.

chapters.title: A Bargain by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rosalind corners Jonah with proof she knows about the ledger; instead of reporting him, she offers passage through the checkpoints in exchange for Elias's page. Beat: uneasy alliance forged from mutual leverage.

chapters.title: The Road to First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Disguised as a sanitary commission, they travel toward the bridge checkpoint at Marrow Ford. Beat: fragile camaraderie; Jonah notices Rosalind counts everything—steps, rations, lies.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A young officer with a photographic memory nearly catches them; Rosalind bluffs using genuine census credentials. Beat: terror and exhilaration; the ledger passes inches from discovery.

chapters.title: Elias, As Remembered
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. By firelight, Rosalind reads her brother's page aloud—wounded, then vanished after questioning. She confesses she suspects he was silenced, not deserted. Beat: grief converts her mission from bureaucratic to sacred.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Dinner
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They shelter with Colonel Brandt, whose name appears in the ledger as the man who ordered omissions. He toasts 'honest men' while Jonah sweats. Beat: dramatic irony tightens like a wire.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A wounded orderly, Private Kessler, recognizes Jonah's handwriting and begs him to add his brother's name. Adding it means opening the ledger at a hostile table. Beat: loyalty vs. self-preservation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Betrayal at Halven
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Kessler, arrested and interrogated, gives up a description of the pair. Rosalind wants to flee alone; Jonah refuses to abandon the ledger—or her. Beat: alliance strains toward breaking.

chapters.title: Into the Marsh Country
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Off the roads now, they cross flooded marshes guided by a smuggler who demands payment Jonah cannot cover. Beat: exhaustion strips both characters to essentials; unexpected tenderness surfaces.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The smuggler demands the ledger itself as payment. Rosalind offers her credentials and future instead; Jonah secretly offers the thing he values most—his own name added to its pages. Beat: identity as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Second checkpoint, now forewarned; a wanted notice describes Rosalind exactly. They split—she walks through openly as bait while Jonah crosses the weir with the ledger. Beat: trust as a deliberate act of courage.

chapters.title: Reunion in Ash
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Detained and questioned, Rosalind talks her way out but learns the tribunal has been postponed indefinitely—truth may arrive too late. Beat: despair; the goalpost moves and hope gutters.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror Ward
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In a requisitioned asylum serving as a depot, Jonah finds a living patient who shouldn't exist: Elias Ashe, alive, broken, and officially dead. Beat: revelation upends everything—some names were omitted to hide survivors.

chapters.title: Elias Speaks
chapters.summary: Elias's POV (brief). Elias recounts the massacre he survived and why Brandt erased the witnesses. Rosalind must choose: expose the crime and endanger her brother, or stay silent and let the dead go uncounted. Beat: loyalty vs. truth at full weight.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The capital gate at dawn, guards checking every satchel. Jonah hides the ledger inside a coffin of a named, honored officer—the one place no one dares search. Beat: audacity as climax approach; hearts hammering.

chapters.title: Surrender at the Gate
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The ruse fails; guards close in. Jonah steps forward, declares himself the ledger-keeper, and draws them off so Rosalind slips through with the pages sewn into her coat. Beat: climax—self-sacrifice as the ultimate act of belonging.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Reads
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Before the tribunal, Rosalind testifies; Elias appears alive to contradict the death rolls. Brandt falls, and every name in the ledger is read aloud into the record. Beat: catharsis; truth spoken has weight at last.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Compass
chapters.summary: Shared epilogue POV. Months later, Jonah—pardoned, his own name finally entered in the record—meets Rosalind where the marsh road begins. She gives him a brass compass engraved with Elias's initials. Beat: resolution—belonging found not in invisibility, but in being counted.
